q: The Lotus Temple in Delhi is a house of worship of which faith?
note: Completed in 1986, it is shaped like a lotus with 27 marble-clad petals.

q: Old Delhi's Khari Baoli is famous as a huge wholesale market for what?
note: Its name comes from a stepwell of brackish, or 'khari', water that once stood there.

q: Which Delhi market is best known as a hub for computer hardware and software?
note: Its tightly packed shops sell everything from laptops to spare parts and printer cartridges.

q: Chandni Chowk was designed in the 1650s by which daughter of Shah Jahan?
note: A canal once ran down its centre, and its reflected moonlight is said to explain 'Chandni'.

q: Which fluffy, saffron-tinged milk-foam dessert is sold on Old Delhi's streets only in winter?
note: Lucknow calls the same dessert malai makhan, and Varanasi calls it malaiyo.

q: Delhi's Jantar Mantar observatory was built by which Rajput ruler?
note: He built five such observatories: Delhi, Jaipur, Ujjain, Varanasi and Mathura.

q: Which old stepwell near Connaught Place appeared in Aamir Khan's film PK?
note: It is a protected monument, about 60 metres long, whose well is now mostly dry.

q: Which architect is credited with designing Delhi's Connaught Place?
note: Named after the Duke of Connaught, it was built between 1929 and 1933.

q: Which British architect designed New Delhi's North and South Block secretariat buildings?
note: He worked alongside Edwin Lutyens on the plan for the new imperial capital.

q: What does the name of Delhi's Hauz Khas mean?
note: The water tank was dug by Alauddin Khalji and later restored by Firoz Shah Tughlaq.

q: Old Delhi's Nai Sarak is best known as a wholesale market for what?
note: Students from across North India come here hunting for cheap textbooks.

q: In which year did the Delhi Metro open its first stretch to passengers?
note: The first line ran between Shahdara and Tis Hazari.

q: Delhi's Red Fort is built mainly from which stone?
note: Every Independence Day, the Prime Minister addresses the nation from its ramparts.

q: Poet Mirza Ghalib's haveli stands in which Old Delhi neighbourhood?
note: Gulzar's 1988 TV serial 'Mirza Ghalib' starred Naseeruddin Shah as the poet.

q: Which 13th-century poet-musician of Delhi is traditionally called the father of qawwali?
note: He was a disciple of the Sufi saint Nizamuddin Auliya and wrote in Persian and Hindavi.

q: What is the formal name of Amritsar's Golden Temple?
note: Its community kitchen serves free meals to tens of thousands of visitors every day.

q: Which crisp stuffed bread, baked in a tandoor, is Amritsar's most famous breakfast?
note: It is usually served with chhole, onion chutney and a big dollop of butter.

q: Which Punjabi women's folk dance is performed to rhythmic clapping and witty couplets called boliyan?
note: Dancers form a circle while one or two at a time step into the middle to perform.

q: Which single-stringed plucked instrument gives Punjabi folk songs their twangy sound?
note: Folk singer Lalchand Yamla Jatt made the tumbi famous.

q: Which Punjab city lends its name to a famously baggy, pleated salwar?
note: Patiala was the capital of one of Punjab's most powerful princely states.

q: Hero Cycles was founded in 1956 in which Punjab city?
note: Ludhiana is also a major hub for hosiery and woollen knitwear.

q: Which Punjab city is a major centre for making sports goods like balls and hockey sticks?
note: Its workshops turn out equipment for cricket, hockey, football and boxing.

q: Which Punjab village is Bhagat Singh's ancestral home and site of his memorial museum?
note: He was actually born in Banga, in present-day Pakistan's Faisalabad district.

q: Which Punjabi writer became the first woman to win the Sahitya Akademi Award, in 1956?
note: Her autobiography is titled 'Raseedi Ticket', meaning revenue stamp.

q: Which Punjabi poet, called 'Birha da Sultan', won the Sahitya Akademi Award for his verse play 'Loona'?
note: His poem 'Ik Kudi Jida Naam Mohabbat' was used in the film Udta Punjab.

q: In Punjabi, whom do you respectfully call 'paaji'?
note: It is also used warmly for any older man, whether friend or stranger.

q: Hola Mohalla, a festival of martial arts displays, is held at which Punjab town?
note: It features mock battles, horse-riding feats and gatka martial-arts displays.

q: Which Indian spin legend, born in Amritsar, was known for his colourful patkas?
note: His left-arm spin took 266 Test wickets.

q: Which ghee-rich winter sweet ball, made with wheat flour and jaggery, is a Punjabi favourite?
note: Packed with dry fruits, pinnis are traditionally made to keep warm through cold months.

q: The Punjab city of Faridkot is named after which Sufi saint?
note: Baba Farid's verses are included in the Guru Granth Sahib.

q: What is the traditional embroidered flat footwear of Punjab called?
note: Classic juttis have no separate left or right and mould to the feet with wear.

q: Which Haryana city is known as the 'City of Weavers'?
note: It is also a big centre for recycling old woollens into blankets and rugs.

q: The Surajkund International Crafts Mela is held every February near which city?
note: Each year a different Indian state is chosen as the fair's theme state.

q: In Haryanvi, what does 'chhori' mean?
note: The male form is 'chhora', meaning boy.

q: The first Indian-born woman to fly in space was born in which Haryana city?
note: She studied aeronautical engineering at Punjab Engineering College in Chandigarh.

q: Haryana's Mughal-era Pinjore Gardens are also known by what name?
note: The terraced gardens were laid out in the 17th century by Nawab Fidai Khan.

q: What is the name of Haryana's traditional folk theatre of songs and dialogue?
note: Pandit Lakhmi Chand is its most celebrated poet-performer.

q: The Murrah, a famous dairy breed from Haryana, is which animal?
note: Murrah buffaloes are recognised by their short, tightly coiled horns.

q: What was Gurugram's official name before 2016?
note: Its Cyber City business district hosts the Indian offices of many global companies.

q: Hisar was founded in the 14th century by which Delhi Sultan?
note: The city's name comes from the Persian word for fort.

q: Which Haryana village is one of the largest known Harappan sites?
note: It lies in Hisar district, with several excavated mounds spread over a wide area.

q: In Haryanvi and Hindi, who is your 'tau'?
note: Villagers also call any respected older man 'tau'.

q: Which is Haryana's only hill station?
note: It lies in Panchkula district and has twin lakes called Tikkar Tal.

q: Which Haryana town is nicknamed 'Mini Cuba' for its boxers?
note: Its boxing club has produced many national and international medallists.

q: Which hill town served as the summer capital of British India?
note: The Kalka–Shimla toy train line opened in 1903 to reach it.

q: Which Himachal valley's Dussehra begins on Vijayadashami, the day celebrations end elsewhere?
note: Hundreds of local deities are carried in palanquins to honour Lord Raghunath.

q: Which steamed wheat bun, stuffed with walnut or poppy-seed paste, is a Himachali speciality?
note: It is usually served hot with ghee and green chutney.

q: What is the traditional Himachali community feast, served on leaf plates, called?
note: It is cooked by hereditary chefs called botis.

q: Which embroidered square cloth, used to cover gifts, is Chamba's famous craft?
note: Its double satin stitch makes both sides of the cloth look the same.

q: Kangra in Himachal Pradesh is famous for which art form?
note: Kangra paintings often show Radha and Krishna in lush green landscapes.

q: What does the name of Spiti's Chandratal mean?
note: The crescent-shaped lake sits at about 4,300 metres.

q: Manali's famous wooden pagoda-style temple is dedicated to which Mahabharata figure?
note: She was Bhima's wife; the temple was built in 1553.

q: Which American-born settler introduced commercial apple farming to Himachal's Kotgarh area?
note: He later took the name Satyanand Stokes and joined India's freedom movement.

q: Which graceful group folk dance, performed in long lines at village fairs, is iconic across Himachal Pradesh?
note: Dancers link arms and move in slow, rhythmic steps to drums and wind instruments.

q: Author Ruskin Bond was born in which Himachal hill town?
note: Born there in 1934, he later made Landour, near Mussoorie, his home.

q: Which Himachal meadow near Dalhousie is nicknamed the 'Mini Switzerland of India'?
note: A Swiss diplomat gave it the nickname in 1992.

q: Which Himachal town is nicknamed the 'Mushroom City of India'?
note: It is home to the national Directorate of Mushroom Research.

q: Which Himachal spot near Baijnath is famous as a paragliding hub?
note: Pilots take off from Billing and land near the village of Bir.

q: Which Uttarakhand town is often called the 'Yoga Capital of the World'?
note: The Beatles stayed at an ashram here in 1968.

q: At which Haridwar ghat does the famous evening Ganga aarti take place?
note: The name means 'steps of Lord Hari'.

q: India's training academy for IAS officers is located in which hill town?
note: The academy is named after former Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri.

q: Which Uttarakhand hill town is often called the 'Lake District of India'?
note: The town wraps around the eye-shaped Naini Lake.

q: Bal mithai, a brown fudge coated with white sugar balls, comes from which Uttarakhand town?
note: Another Almora favourite is singori, khoya wrapped in a leaf cone.

q: Besides Garhwali, which is the other major hill language of Uttarakhand?
note: Kumaoni is spoken in the eastern hills around Almora, Nainital and Pithoragarh.

q: The Indian Military Academy, which trains army officers, is in which city?
note: It was established in 1932; cadets pass out in front of its Chetwode Hall.

q: Which of these is NOT one of Uttarakhand's Char Dham shrines?
note: The fourth Char Dham shrine is Badrinath, dedicated to Vishnu.

q: Which Uttarakhand resort near Joshimath (now Jyotirmath) is famous for skiing?
note: It hosted the first South Asian Winter Games in 2011.

q: In the Chipko movement of the 1970s, what did villagers hug to protect them?
note: It began in Chamoli district in 1973; Gaura Devi led women at Reni village.

q: Which Chhayavad-era Hindi poet was born in Kausani, Uttarakhand?
note: In 1968 he became the first Hindi poet to win the Jnanpith Award.

q: Which sword dance, performed in Kumaoni wedding processions, comes from Uttarakhand?
note: Dancers carry swords and shields to the beat of the dhol and damau.

q: What is Kumaon's ritual folk art, drawn in white rice paste on red ochre, called?
note: Designs are drawn by hand on floors, doorsteps and walls during festivals.

q: Which Uttarakhand cantonment town is home to the Garhwal Rifles Regimental Centre?
note: Nearby Ranikhet is home to the Kumaon Regiment's centre.

q: Which milk sweet is Mathura most famous for?
note: Mathura pedas get their brown colour from slow-roasting khoya until it caramelises.

q: Which polite phrase, meaning 'you first', symbolises Lucknow's famous etiquette?
note: The city's refined manners are summed up in one word: tehzeeb.

q: Lucknow's Bara Imambara is famous for which maze of passages?
note: The Bara Imambara was built in 1784 partly as a famine-relief project.

q: Which UP city is famous for making glass bangles?
note: Its glass industry also makes chandeliers and decorative glassware.

q: Which UP city is famous for making locks?
note: Its lock-making tradition earned it the nickname 'Tala Nagri'.

q: Which UP town is known as India's 'Carpet City'?
note: Bhadohi's hand-knotted carpets carry a GI tag.

q: Kannauj, UP's perfume town, is famous for which traditional oil-based perfume?
note: Its 'mitti attar' is distilled from baked earth to capture the smell of first rain.

q: Which Agra tomb, built by Nur Jahan for her father, is nicknamed the 'Baby Taj'?
note: It was completed in the 1620s, before the Taj Mahal was built.

q: Agra's Taj Mahal stands on the bank of which river?
note: The Mehtab Bagh garden across the river offers a classic view of the Taj.

q: At Prayagraj's Triveni Sangam, the Ganga and Yamuna meet which mythical river?
note: Kumbh Mela pilgrims gather to bathe at this confluence.

q: Which Varanasi ghat hosts the city's grandest evening Ganga aarti?
note: Priests perform the aarti in unison with large brass lamps as crowds watch from boats.

q: Which singer, born in Faizabad, was celebrated as 'Mallika-e-Ghazal'?
note: She was posthumously awarded the Padma Bhushan in 1975.

q: Hockey wizard Dhyan Chand was born in which city?
note: His family later settled in Jhansi, the city most associated with him.

q: Which city's paan is celebrated in the Don (1978) song 'Khaike Paan ___wala'?
note: Kishore Kumar sang it, to music by Kalyanji-Anandji.

q: Surdas composed his Krishna poetry in which dialect of the Mathura–Vrindavan region?
note: Braj Bhasha was once the main literary language of North Indian devotional poetry.

q: Lucknow is home to a famous gharana of which classical dance?
note: Pandit Birju Maharaj was the best-known exponent of the Lucknow gharana.

q: At which UP town is the Buddha believed to have attained mahaparinirvana?
note: Its Mahaparinirvana Temple houses a reclining Buddha statue about 6 metres long.

q: Which UP folk theatre form, with Kanpur and Hathras styles, is known for song and melodrama?
note: Performances traditionally used the booming nagara drum to draw crowds.

q: Kajri, a folk song form sung in the monsoon, is most associated with which UP city?
note: Varanasi singers like Girija Devi also made kajri famous.

q: According to the 1966 song 'Jhumka Gira Re', in which city's bazaar did the jhumka fall?
note: In 2020 Bareilly installed a giant jhumka sculpture at a city crossing.

q: Malihabad, near Lucknow, is famous for which mango variety?
note: The Malihabadi Dasheri carries a GI tag.

q: Which grand Lucknow gateway is also called the 'Turkish Gate'?
note: Built in 1784, the same year as the Bara Imambara, it stands about 18 metres tall.

q: In Rajasthan's classic trio, dal and baati are served with which crumbly sweet?
note: Churma is made by crushing baati or rotis with ghee and sugar or jaggery.

q: The snack brand Haldiram's began as a shop in which city?
note: Bikaner is also famous for its crisp Bikaneri bhujia.

q: Which fiery red mutton curry is a Rajasthani royal classic?
note: Its red colour traditionally comes from Mathania chillies.

q: Which Rajasthani dish is made from dried desert beans and berries?
note: Sangri are the dried pods of the khejri tree; ker is a wild desert berry.

q: Jaipur's Hawa Mahal is popularly called the 'Palace of' what?
note: Its many latticed windows let royal women watch street festivities unseen.

q: What are Rajasthan's long painted cloth scrolls, unrolled by bards to narrate folk-hero legends, called?
note: Performers called bhopas sing the story at night while lighting up each scene with a lamp.

q: What is Rajasthan's wave-patterned tie-dye fabric called?
note: 'Lehar' means wave; leheriya is especially popular during Teej.

q: Which UNESCO-listed Rajasthani folk dance mimics the swaying movements of a snake?
note: UNESCO added Kalbelia songs and dances to its intangible heritage list in 2010.

q: Which ancient Rajasthani bowed string instrument is named after the Ramayana's ten-headed king?
note: Its body is traditionally a coconut shell or gourd covered with skin, with a bamboo neck.

q: Complete the Rajasthani folk song line: 'Kesariya balam, padharo mhare ___'.
note: The line means 'Saffron beloved, come to my land'.

q: Which respectful Rajasthani greeting is used much like 'hello'?
note: It is usually returned with the same words.

q: Which 16th-century Rajput princess from Merta became famous for her devotional songs to Krishna?
note: She married into the royal family of Mewar.

q: What was the name of Maharana Pratap's famous horse?
note: A memorial to the horse, Chetak Smarak, stands in Rajsamand district.

q: Chittorgarh's Vijay Stambh was built by which Mewar ruler?
note: The nine-storey tower was built in the 1440s to mark a victory over Malwa.

q: Which Rajasthan fort's immense wall is nicknamed the 'Great Wall of India'?
note: Its walls run for about 36 km around the fort complex.

q: The Satyajit Ray film 'Sonar Kella' is set around which Rajasthan fort?
note: Ray based the 1974 film on his own novel of the same name.

q: Pushkar is famous for one of the very few temples dedicated to which Hindu god?
note: Pushkar Lake beside the town is ringed by about 52 ghats.

q: What is the mirror-encrusted hall inside Jaipur's Amer Fort called?
note: Its mirrored ceiling is said to sparkle like a starry sky when lit by a single candle.

q: The white marble of the Taj Mahal came mainly from which Rajasthan town?
note: Makrana marble was also used for Kolkata's Victoria Memorial.

q: Which spring festival sees Rajasthani women worship Goddess Gauri with songs and processions?
note: Jaipur marks it with a royal procession starting from the City Palace.

q: Kishangarh's famous 'Bani Thani' painting is often called India's version of which masterpiece?
note: It was painted by Nihal Chand in the 18th century.

q: Silao, near Nalanda, is famous for which flaky, many-layered sweet?
note: It is made from layers of wheat dough, fried crisp and soaked in sugar syrup.

q: Gaya is famous for which crunchy sesame-and-jaggery winter sweet?
note: It is eaten especially around Makar Sankranti.

q: The Bodhi Tree, under which the Buddha attained enlightenment at Bodh Gaya, is which kind of tree?
note: A sapling from it was planted at Anuradhapura in the 3rd century BCE.

q: Which Sikh Guru was born in Patna in 1666?
note: Takht Sri Patna Sahib marks his birthplace.

q: Patna's beehive-shaped Golghar was built to serve as what?
note: Built in 1786, it has spiral staircases winding up its outside.

q: Which Bihar city is nicknamed 'Silk City' for its tussar silk?
note: The ruins of the ancient Vikramashila university lie nearby.

q: Which ancient Bihar city is often called one of the world's earliest republics?
note: It was the capital of the Licchavis; Mahavira was born nearby.

q: Which Bihar fair, held around Kartik Purnima where the Gandak meets the Ganga, is famous for livestock?
note: It is also known as the Harihar Kshetra Mela.

q: Which temple at Bodh Gaya marks the spot of the Buddha's enlightenment?
note: Emperor Ashoka is said to have built the first shrine at the site.

q: Ustad Bismillah Khan was born in which Bihar town?
note: He later made Varanasi his lifelong home.

q: Which folk singer, beloved for her Chhath songs, was called 'Bihar Kokila'?
note: She also sang 'Kahe Toh Se Sajna' in Maine Pyar Kiya (1989).

q: Which playwright, called the 'Shakespeare of Bhojpuri', created the Bidesiya folk theatre?
note: His plays told of migrant workers and the families they left behind.

q: The medieval poet Vidyapati wrote his famous songs mainly in which language?
note: Maithili is one of the 22 languages in the Constitution's Eighth Schedule.

q: Bihar's Mithila region is famous for which puffed water-lily seed snack, also called fox nut?
note: Mithila Makhana received a GI tag in 2022.

q: Muzaffarpur is famous for which fruit, whose local variety is called Shahi?
note: Shahi Litchi received its GI tag in 2018.

q: Chandigarh's main shopping plaza, the city's commercial heart, is in which sector?
note: Its pedestrian plaza, with a fountain and clock tower, is a favourite hangout spot.

q: Who created Chandigarh's Rock Garden from industrial and urban waste?
note: He began building it secretly on government land around 1957.

q: Which man-made lake at the foot of the Shivalik hills is Chandigarh's favourite promenade?
note: It was created in 1958 by damming a seasonal stream.

q: Which sector number did Chandigarh's original plan famously skip, until Mani Majra was given it in 2020?
note: The number is widely reported to have been left out of the original plan as unlucky.

q: Chandigarh takes its name from a nearby temple of which goddess?
note: The Chandi Mandir temple lies just outside the city, in Panchkula.

q: Which Le Corbusier monument is the official emblem of Chandigarh?
note: The giant metal hand turns in the wind like a weathervane.

q: What is the long, loose woollen cloak worn in Kashmiri winters called?
note: Its roomy cut lets wearers keep a warm fire pot tucked inside.

q: What is the wicker-covered clay fire pot Kashmiris keep under their cloaks in winter?
note: The clay bowl inside holds glowing charcoal embers.

q: Srinagar's Shalimar Bagh was built by which Mughal emperor?
note: He built it in 1619 for his wife, Nur Jahan.

q: Which majestic tree, whose leaves turn fiery red in autumn, is iconic in Kashmir?
note: Many of Kashmir's oldest chinars were planted in Mughal times.

q: Which velvety pounded-mutton meatball in yogurt gravy traditionally ends a wazwan feast?
note: Its red-gravy cousin in the same feast is called rista.

q: Which Kashmir resort is famous for skiing and its high gondola cable car?
note: Its name means 'meadow of flowers'.

q: Which 14th-century Kashmiri mystic poet is famous for her verses called 'vakhs'?
note: Her verses are among the earliest known works in the Kashmiri language.

q: At Ladakh's monastery festivals, monks perform the sacred Cham dance wearing what?
note: Cham dances act out the triumph of good over evil to drums, cymbals and long horns.

q: What is the all-purpose Ladakhi greeting for hello, goodbye and thank you?
note: Visitors quickly learn it, since locals use it for almost every exchange.

q: Which double-humped camels can be ridden in Ladakh's Nubra Valley?
note: They roam the sand dunes around Hunder village.

q: Zanskar's winter 'Chadar Trek' is a walk along a frozen what?
note: 'Chadar' means blanket, for the sheet of ice that forms over the Zanskar river.

q: Which spot near Leh seems to pull vehicles uphill, thanks to an optical illusion?
note: The surrounding slopes make a gentle downhill stretch look like an uphill road.
